Dana (Sales): Quick heads-up — NexaCare POC reporting repeated 429s when running a scripted demo. Happening around minute 5 of their 10-min scenario. Tenant header: X-Tenant-ID: nexa-42. Can someone triage?

Ravi (Platform SE): Thanks. What endpoint/model are they calling and do we have the raw response body / headers? Also were they using streaming?

Dana (Sales): They hit POST /v1/chat/complete (model: redwood-multi-8k) non-streaming. Customer pasted this response: 

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "error": "rate_limit",
  "message": "burst quota exceeded for route",
  "retry_after": 18
}
X-RateLimit-Limit: 1200
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 18
```

They said they were running 60 concurrent sessions with max_tokens=400 and short prompts.

Chen (SRE): Pulling infra logs for nexa-42 now. Note: hosted tenant, default burst policy is token-equivalent sliding window (60s). If many concurrent with high max_tokens, token accounting can blow out quickly.

Pat (Support): Log excerpt from edge (ordered):
```
2026-04-02T09:03:12Z tenant=nexa-42 route=/v1/chat/complete concurrent=62 tokens_est=380 tokens_window=60 tokens_used_window=23560 rlimit=1200 remain=0
2026-04-02T09:03:17Z tenant=nexa-42 429 burst-limit exceeded
```
That aligns with their report. Daily token quota for tenant = 5,000,000 so not a daily limit. It's burst cap.

Ravi (Platform SE): Two parallel paths: (1) customer-side tweaks — lower max_tokens to 200, switch to streaming, and use client concurrency limit (e.g., 30); (2) short-lived platform increase to burst cap for the demo. Which preferred?

Dana (Sales): Customer wants a clean 1-hour exec demo tomorrow. Can we allow a temporary bump for the demo window? Nina — commercial ok?

Nina (AE): NexaCare is a strategic midmarket lead. Approve temporary bump to 1500 for 1 hour during demo, provided we collect metrics and attach to the opportunity. I'll log approval in the CRM.

Chen (SRE): I'll put a scoped change with a TTL and enable verbose token sampling. Plan: bump per-route burst cap for tenant nexa-42 from 1200 -> 1500 for 3600s starting 2026-04-03T16:00:00Z. Add alert if 5xx or 429 >1% over 5m.

RateBot: Change request queued: CR#SR-9301.

Pat (Support): Applying change now (rc-id: bump-9301). Patch:
```
PATCH /config/tenants/nexa-42
set per_route_burst_cap=1500 (ttl=3600s)
set debug.token_sampling=on
```

RateBot: Change applied by Pat. CR#SR-9301 status=applied. AuditTrail updated.

Dana (Sales): Passed timings to NexaCare. They will run demo at 16:15. Also sent them client snippet to throttle concurrency + enable streaming.

Ravi (Platform SE): Snippet we gave them:
```
// simple concurrency gate + streaming example
const pLimit = createLimiter(30);
await pLimit.run(() => fetch('/v1/chat/complete', { body: JSON.stringify({max_tokens:200, stream:true}) }));
```

Chen (SRE): Monitoring during the window: peak concurrent reached ~140, no 429s observed. Token sampling shows average per-request tokens 320 -> reduced from earlier estimate.

Pat (Support): After TTL expiry (16:15 +1h), config reverted to per_route_burst_cap=1200 and we saw 429s resume under their same scripted load within ~3 minutes. Collected screenshots & logs and attached to SR-9301.

Nina (AE): Customer exec satisfied with demo. They've asked for Dedicated sizing guidance. I'll start AE handoff and include the metrics.

Chen (SRE): Ops notes: recommend adding a POC checklist entry advising streaming/non-blocking clients, default client concurrency cap sample, and a documented process for demo-cap bumps. Also recommend we consider per-tenant temporary autoscale for trials.

Ravi (Platform SE): Agreed — will draft docs snippet and a template email for requesting demo bumps.

Dana (Sales): Thanks everyone. Closing this thread — will follow up if customer has further questions. :white_check_mark:
